title: Fireworks, Then Football. The World Cup Takes Over the Fourth of July — and NRIs Have the Best Seats in the House.
excerpt: Canada face Morocco in Houston at 1 PM ET. France meet Paraguay in Philadelphia at 5 PM ET. For Indian Americans, a holiday spent watching the world's biggest tournament on American soil is an experience without precedent.
body:
The Fourth of July has always been about spectacle. This year, for the first time in the tournament's 96-year history, the FIFA World Cup is part of it.

Two Round of 16 matches land on American Independence Day — Canada versus Morocco at NRG Stadium in Houston (1 PM ET / 10 AM PT), and Paraguay versus France at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia (5 PM ET / 2 PM PT). The timing is deliberate. FIFA wanted this. America wanted this. And for the estimated 4.5 million Indian Americans spread across cities like Houston, Philadelphia, New York, and Chicago, this is a holiday unlike anything that came before.

## The Afternoon Kick: Canada vs Morocco, Houston

The first knockout game of the day is a collision between two of the tournament's best stories.

Canada have already exceeded every expectation. Before this World Cup, they had never won a knockout match. That changed when Stephen Eustáquio scored in the 92nd minute against South Africa to send Les Rouges through to the Round of 16 for the first time. A win today would put them in the quarterfinals — territory no Canadian men's team has ever touched.

Morocco, though, are a different proposition. The Atlas Lions finished level on points with Brazil in Group C, then knocked out the Netherlands on penalties in the Round of 32. Their 2022 semi-final run was no fluke — this is a team built on defensive discipline and devastating counter-attacks, with Real Madrid's Achraf Hakimi controlling the right flank. He leads the team with 11 chances created and five shots on goal.

Houston's NRG Stadium — home of the NFL's Houston Texans — holds over 72,000 for the tournament. The city has one of America's largest South Asian populations, and the blend of World Cup energy and Fourth of July celebration will be unlike anything the city has seen.

## The Evening Feature: France vs Paraguay, Philadelphia

The bigger name arrives later.

France dismantled Sweden 3-0 in the Round of 32, with Kylian Mbappé scoring twice to become the leading goalscorer in World Cup knockout history. Les Bleus have been clinical throughout the group stage, and Didier Deschamps' side are among the favourites to lift the trophy on July 19.

Paraguay, however, are the tournament's most improbable survivors. They shocked Germany on penalties in the Round of 32 — the first time Die Mannschaft have been eliminated before the last 16 since 2018 — and are playing with the freedom of a team with absolutely nothing to lose. That result cost Julian Nagelsmann his job and brought Jürgen Klopp in as Germany's new manager.

Philadelphia's Lincoln Financial Field will be packed for the evening kickoff. For the Indian American community in the tri-state area — one of the densest concentrations of South Asians anywhere outside the subcontinent — the match is a natural extension of the day's festivities.

## What Comes Next

The winners of today's matches are on a collision course. They meet in the quarterfinals on Thursday, July 9 — meaning one of Canada, Morocco, France, or Paraguay will be among the last eight teams standing.

Sunday brings two more blockbusters: Brazil vs Norway at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey (4 PM ET), and England vs Mexico at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City (8 PM ET). Monday delivers the fixtures the world has been waiting for — Portugal vs Spain in Arlington, Texas (3 PM ET), and USA vs Belgium in Seattle (8 PM ET).

## Where to Watch

All Round of 16 matches are on FOX (English) and Telemundo (Spanish) in the United States, with streaming on Peacock Premium and Fubo TV. For NRIs in the UK, ITV carries coverage; in Canada, TSN and RDS.

The World Cup has never been on American soil on the Fourth of July before. It will never feel quite like this again. Between the barbecues and the bottle rockets, the bracket beckons.
